subject: Specifiying a space-time interaction random effects by rgeneric 0 and control.group

messages.author: e9ab831d77228443
messages.subject: Specifiying a space-time interaction random effects by rgeneric 0 and control.group
parts:
Hi INLA Groups,

I hope you have spent a happy Christmas.
I want to specifiy an interaction of space and time components by analogy the IV interaction from Held.
The spatial random effect (u) reads,  u \sim MVN \left ( 0, \sigma_{u}^{2}(I-W)(I-{W}') \right )
I is an identity matrix and W is a spatia adjacent matrix, and there is not spatial strength coefficent in the covariance matrix.

The temporal random effects (t) follows a first-order autoregressive process.

In this context, I would like to know, whether we can specifiy an interaction between u and t following the specification of IV interaction?

I try the following code:

library("DClusterm")
data(brainNM)
library(INLA)

nm.adj <- poly2nb(brainst@sp)
adj.mat <- as(nb2mat(nm.adj, style = "B"), "Matrix")

brainst @ data$ID3<- as.numeric(brainst @ data$ID)
brainst @ data$ID.Year <- brainst @ data$Year - 1973 + 1


Q_sar<- (Diagonal(nrow(adj.mat), x = 1) - adj.mat) %*% t(Diagonal(nrow(adj.mat), x = 1) - adj.mat)

brain.st4.sar1 <- inla(Observed ~ 1 + 
                        f(ID3, model = "generic0", Cmatrix = Q_sar,
                          group = ID.Year, control.group = list(model = "ar1")
                          ),
                      data = brainst@data, E = Expected, verbose = T, family = "poisson",
                      control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE, link = 1))
summary(brain.st4.sar1)

If the code is correct, how to specifiy prior for this interaction term?

Thanks in advance.
All the best,
Charles

constraints can be high.

Thank you for your reply.

As you mentioned that I have to manually build type IV interaction, I have met several questions here.

f(ID3, model="generic0", 
  Cmatrix=kronecker(Q_AR1,Q_sar), 
  rankdef= ?,
  constr=TRUE, 
  extraconstr=list(A= ? , e=rep(0,n+t)))

3. Is it necessary to add "extraconstr="?

Hi,

For type IV, please cyheck out the kn4formula in http://www.leg.ufpr.br/~elias/cursos/br2015/r/cwb-example.R

In order to use kronecker models, e.g., 'ar1' with 'besag' you can use
 f(idx.space, model='besag', graph=..., 
     group=idx.time, control.group=list(model='ar1'))

there is no rank deficiency for 'ar1'.

best regards,
Elias

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Specifiying a space-time interaction random effects by rgeneric 0 and control.group
parts:
Hi Leo,

technically speaking, the stochastic PDE models of order 2 are closely related to discrete domain simultaneous auto-regression (SAR) models of the type you describe. These SPDE models have discretised precisions with the same structure as the discrete SAR models, so inla.spde2.generic() could in principle be used to construct more general versions (that could include a dependence strength parameter). However, in your special case where there is only a global precision scaling parameter, the generic0 approach that is in your code is the most efficient solution.

The code looks fine, except that, if I understand correctly, your I-W matrix has row-sum zero, Is your precision (I-W)(I-W)' or (I-W)'(I-W) ?
For example, if the purely spatial model is invariant to adding a constant, then the kronecker product model will be invariant to adding a different constant to each time step.
Using rank-deficient models as building blocks can be a pain, as you need to keep track of the rank-deficiencies, and because introducing constraints changes the model interpretation and behaviour;
for example, imposing a sum-to-zero constraint on each time step means the one will likely need to add a separate time-process to the model to allow it to vary usefully across time.
Alternatively, if invariance to adding a different global constant across space for each time point is what you want, then you can leave the g=kronecker model as it is, and instead remove the global intercept from the model, since otherwise it will be non-identifiable.

Finn

parts: Hi Finn,
Thank you for your reply.

I have applied inla.spde2.matern, but I have never used inla.spde2.generic(). Is there any useful document introducting this "inla.spde.generic()"?

In particular, as you mentioned dependence strength parameter in SAR models, I know that this can be done through rgeneric1 related wrapper functions. But how this can be done by inla.spde2.generic()? Then, the dependence strength parameter is time varying? Because in inla.spde2.matern case, there is not a dependence strength parameter.

I-W matrix has row-sum zero and the precision reads (I-W)(I-W)'.

Thank you for your tips in terms of the indentifiability issue, I think that I will leave the kronecker model and remove global intercept.

在 2020年12月28日星期一 UTC+1下午11:37:06，Finn Lindgren写道：

Hi Leo,

technically speaking, the stochastic PDE models of order 2 are closely related to discrete domain simultaneous auto-regression (SAR) models of the type you describe. These SPDE models have discretised precisions with the same structure as the discrete SAR models, so inla.spde2.generic() could in principle be used to construct more general versions (that could include a dependence strength parameter). However, in your special case where there is only a global precision scaling parameter, the generic0 approach that is in your code is the most efficient solution.

The code looks fine, except that, if I understand correctly, your I-W matrix has row-sum zero, Is your precision (I-W)(I-W)' or (I-W)'(I-W) ?
For example, if the purely spatial model is invariant to adding a constant, then the kronecker product model will be invariant to adding a different constant to each time step.
Using rank-deficient models as building blocks can be a pain, as you need to keep track of the rank-deficiencies, and because introducing constraints changes the model interpretation and behaviour;
for example, imposing a sum-to-zero constraint on each time step means the one will likely need to add a separate time-process to the model to allow it to vary usefully across time.
Alternatively, if invariance to adding a different global constant across space for each time point is what you want, then you can leave the g=kronecker model as it is, and instead remove the global intercept from the model, since otherwise it will be non-identifiable.

Finn

All the best,
Charles   

在 2020年12月28日星期一 UTC+1下午5:10:55，Elias T. Krainski写道：

Hi,

For type IV, please cyheck out the kn4formula in http://www.leg.ufpr.br/~elias/cursos/br2015/r/cwb-example.R

 f(idx.space, model='besag', graph=...,

there is no rank deficiency for 'ar1'.

best regards,
Elias

Basically we have that
(I - rW)(I-rW)' = I -rW-rW'+r^2WW'
and one has to consider M0 = I, M1 = -(W + W') and M2 = WW' and to reparametrize it in order to have B0, B1 and B2 accordingly.
Elias

在 2020年12月28日星期一 UTC+1下午11:37:06，Finn Lindgren写道：

Hi Leo,

technically speaking, the stochastic PDE models of order 2 are closely related to discrete domain simultaneous auto-regression (SAR) models of the type you describe. These SPDE models have discretised precisions with the same structure as the discrete SAR models, so inla.spde2.generic() could in principle be used to construct more general versions (that could include a dependence strength parameter). However, in your special case where there is only a global precision scaling parameter, the generic0 approach that is in your code is the most efficient solution.

The code looks fine, except that, if I understand correctly, your I-W matrix has row-sum zero, Is your precision (I-W)(I-W)' or (I-W)'(I-W) ?
For example, if the purely spatial model is invariant to adding a constant, then the kronecker product model will be invariant to adding a different constant to each time step.
Using rank-deficient models as building blocks can be a pain, as you need to keep track of the rank-deficiencies, and because introducing constraints changes the model interpretation and behaviour;
for example, imposing a sum-to-zero constraint on each time step means the one will likely need to add a separate time-process to the model to allow it to vary usefully across time.
Alternatively, if invariance to adding a different global constant across space for each time point is what you want, then you can leave the g=kronecker model as it is, and instead remove the global intercept from the model, since otherwise it will be non-identifiable.

Finn
